calls.reason: CDO Magazine documents successive competitive price cuts by ByteDance, Alibaba and Baidu, while Stanford reports converging model performance. Together these support the claimed competitive pressure, though Epoch leaves global price-drop causes uncertain.
Stanford documents narrowing performance gaps, but does not establish that technical advantages are essentially absent or that an exclusive focus on LLMs caused convergence.

The St. Louis Fed shows elevated investment in broad technology categories, not the economy's share devoted to larger LLMs. The packet also lacks evidence that recipients principally pursue the same scaling strategy.

CB Insights reports a funding surge driven by foundation-model development, with LLM developers taking the three largest rounds. Anthropic's rise from a $3.5 billion to a $13 billion round reinforces the ordinary reading of growing investment.
Anthropic's filing establishes its losses, but the packet provides no representative evidence covering most LLM developers. One company's loss history cannot establish the claimed majority.
